matches.quote: The novelty framing overstates the prior consensus. The abstract says STT in AFMTJs "has been assumed non-existent". The paper itself cites theoretical predictions of spin-transfer torque
Heating, spin-orbit torque from the leads, Oersted fields and thermoelectric effects are not excluded as the switching drive. The stack has 5 nm Pt next to both PtMn3 layers
discuss why a junction with an amorphous barrier and polycrystalline electrodes would exceed the TMR of epitaxial Mn3Pt AFMTJs (ref. 12)
The device stack is deposited at room temperature without annealing (Methods), which usually gives a chemically disordered A1 phase with a different magnetic structure.
The 363% value comes from one of 36 devices. Fig. 2b shows that 23 of the 36 devices have TMR below 100%
The NV sample... is an epitaxial (100) PtMn3 film... The device layers are polycrystalline, (111)-textured and grown at room temperature on Pt, without annealing
Several things are not reported: ... whether switching and TMR come back on cooling to 300 K... provide a finer temperature series... on several devices, a reversibility check
The device data also contradict the claim that only pillars comparable to or smaller than the domain size switch abruptly... some 50–75 nm pillars switch gradually.
The two resistance states are not shown to be magnetic (octupole) states rather than resistive switching of the MgO barrier.
The paper does not report: - the number of consecutive cycles per device; - cycle-to-cycle distributions of R_high, R_low and I_c
No device shows a field-swept R(H) loop... Show in-plane and out-of-plane R(H) loops... on devices that also switch with current, reaching the same two resistance levels.
The authors should provide, for the device stack itself: ... the composition, by EDS, RBS, XRF or XPS
Reading the fitted lines in Fig. 2d gives J_c0 ≈ 190 MA/cm²... for AP→P, and J_c0 ≈ 130 MA/cm²... for P→AP... the asymmetry is not discussed.
Give the pillar diameter and RA for the devices in Fig. 2c and Fig. 2d... whether devices degrade or break down after repeated multi-volt pulses

notes: C7 is marked partly because P9 challenges the claim that STT in AFMTJs was unexpected by citing prior theoretical predictions (refs. 44-47) rather than refs. 11-13 and Onsager reciprocity. C12 is marked partly because P13 asks for the measured composition/stoichiometry of the PtMn3 layers but not whether they were co-sputtered or grown from an alloy target. C15 is marked partly because P5 and P10 ask about the polarity asymmetry of switching currents in Fig. 2d and Extended Data Fig. 1 rather than Fig. 2a. For C14, P1 notes systematic variation of RA with pillar diameter and possible pinholes, but does not specifically argue that 2 nm MgO should have a higher intrinsic RA than 1-10 Ohm*um^2.
